title: Check yourself: method parameters and return types

questions.stem: A helper is declared `static int count(Object... items) { return items.length; }`. A caller has `String[] names = {"ana", "ben", "cy"}` and `int[] scores = {7, 9, 4}`. What do `count(names)` and `count(scores)` return?

options.text: 3 and 3, since the String[] and the int[] are each spread into the items array
options.says: an int[] is not an Object[], so it can't be the items array; it becomes its single element

options.text: 3 and 1, since the String[] is spread into the items array and the int[] becomes one element of it
options.says: a String[] fits Object[] and is passed as the array itself; an int[] is one Object, so the compiler wraps it in a new array of one

options.text: 1 and 3, since the String[] becomes one element of the items array and the int[] is spread into it
options.says: a String[] fits Object[] and is passed as the array itself, while an int[] can't be an Object[] and is wrapped as one element

options.text: 1 and 1, since the String[] and the int[] each become one element of the items array
options.says: the compiler builds a new array only when the argument doesn't already fit Object[]; a String[] does

origin.section: A Varargs Parameter Is an Array: the Caller Can Pass Its Own, or null

questions.stem: A library has `static <T> T[] newest(T... events) { return Arrays.copyOf(events, 2); }` and `static <T> T[] latest(T a, T b, T c) { return newest(a, b, c); }`. A caller writes `Instant[] y = latest(i1, i2, i3);`. What happens?

options.text: It returns two Instants, since the array built inside latest is an Instant[]
options.says: the array for newest is built inside latest, where T is a type variable erased to Object, so it is an Object[]

options.text: It returns two Instants, since the copy that Arrays.copyOf makes is an Instant[]
options.says: Arrays.copyOf keeps the runtime type of the array it copies, which here is Object[]

options.text: It throws ClassCastException at the caller's assignment, since the array built inside latest is an Object[]
options.says: inside latest T is erased, so the varargs array is an Object[]; it travels back as T[] and the cast the compiler inserted at the assignment to Instant[] fails

options.text: It throws ClassCastException inside Arrays.copyOf, since the copy that Arrays.copyOf makes can't be a T[]
options.says: copyOf copies an Object[] without complaint; the cast that fails is the one at the caller's assignment

origin.section: A Generic Varargs Array Has the Erased Type, So Handing It Out Fails Somewhere Else

questions.stem: An interface `Loader` declares `byte[] load(String key) throws IOException;`. `MemoryLoader` implements it as `public byte[] load(String key) { return cache.get(key); }`. Another class has `int size() { Loader loader = new MemoryLoader(); return loader.load("k").length; }`. What does javac do?

options.text: It accepts the code, since MemoryLoader.load, which the call runs, declares no exception
options.says: what a caller must catch comes from the type it calls through, here Loader, not from the object

options.text: It accepts the code, since Loader.load, which the call names, is implemented with no exception
options.says: dropping the clause helps only callers that hold a MemoryLoader; callers holding a Loader still see IOException

options.text: It rejects the code, since Loader.load, which the call names, declares an IOException
options.says: the declared type of the reference decides which checked exceptions the call can throw

options.text: It rejects the code, since MemoryLoader.load, which the call runs, leaves out the IOException
options.says: an override may declare fewer checked exceptions than the method it overrides, or none; the error is the call through Loader

origin.section: An Override May Narrow the Return Type and the Checked Exceptions, Never Widen Them

questions.stem: `Document` has `Document copy()`. `Invoice extends Document` overrides it as `Invoice copy()`, and `DraftInvoice extends Invoice` overrides it as `Document copy()`. What does javac say?

options.text: Both classes compile, since each copy() returns Document or a subtype, as Document.copy() declares
options.says: DraftInvoice.copy() overrides Invoice.copy(), so it has to return Invoice or a subtype of it

options.text: Neither class compiles, since each copy() returns a type other than the copy() it overrides
options.says: an override's return type may be the same as, or a subtype of, the overridden method's, so Invoice's narrower type compiles

options.text: Only Invoice fails, since its copy() returns a type narrower than Document, which Document.copy() declares
options.says: a reference return type may narrow to a subtype (a covariant return), so Invoice compiles; DraftInvoice is the one that fails

options.text: Only DraftInvoice fails, since its copy() returns a type wider than Invoice, which Invoice.copy() declares
options.says: Invoice narrows Document to Invoice, which is allowed; DraftInvoice widens Invoice back to Document, which is not

origin.section: An Override May Narrow the Return Type and the Checked Exceptions, Never Widen Them
